title: Prenatal Chronic Noise Exposure Meta-analysis
text:
0.1 Current status
This Quarto book is the reproducible analysis record for the prenatal chronic noise exposure meta-analysis. It is intentionally separate from the older book/ directory, which contains material adapted from the music and rodent meta-analysis.
The workflow is being developed in this order:
The raw extraction file is never overwritten. Reproducible outputs are written to Data/derived/, Data/audits/, and Data/dictionaries/.
The first chapter implements data wrangling and validation. The lnRR chapter is the next stage and currently records the decisions already agreed for the primary and sensitivity analyses.

title: 2  Data wrangling and central-tendency estimates
text:
2.1 Purpose and data lineage
This chapter turns the reviewed extraction database into the analysis-ready table used from Chapter 2 onward.
The starting point is outputs/019ff719-4f39-7b31-8dee-189f2b3ff628/PCN_data_v10_clean.csv. That file is the endpoint of the cross-checking and correction work already completed outside this book (column names, category labels, the offspring_age_class variable defined in the protocol deviation addendum of 18 August 2026, and the gest_window re-label of gest_stage_ex_new). This chapter does not repeat that work, and it does not override any reported mean or SD: for 176 of 207 arms per outcome, c_sd/ex_sd is the value already extracted from the study (or from metaDigitise) and is carried through unchanged. Only two situations produce a new number in R, and both use methods already documented in c_se_derivation/ex_se_derivation:
The standard error (se_final) is calculated the same way for every arm: where an SE was already reported (65 of 207 arms), that reported value is used unchanged; where it was not (142 of 207 arms), it is calculated as SD/sqrt(n) using the mean/SD from the two bullets above. This is the same formula the extraction team already used to populate c_se_analysis/ex_se_analysis, so this chapter’s independent R recalculation is then cross-checked against those columns rather than replacing them. Concretely, this chapter:
As in the original extraction, every derived value keeps a label recording how it was obtained, so a reported statistic and a calculated one are never visually indistinguishable.

2.2 Import the raw extraction file
The raw CSV contains duplicate higher_better_notes headers and one empty header. They are resolved by position before the remaining column names are standardized to lower-case snake_case. The source CSV itself is not edited.

clean_column_names <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("([a-z0-9])([A-Z])", "\\1_\\2", x)
  x <- tolower(x)
  x <- gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "_", x)
  x <- gsub("^_+|_+$", "", x)
  make.unique(x, sep = "_")
}

db_raw <- readr::read_csv(
  raw_path,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  name_repair = "minimal"
)

raw_row_count <- nrow(db_raw)
raw_column_count <- ncol(db_raw)

source_names <- names(db_raw)

duplicate_note_columns <- which(source_names == "higher_better_notes")
if (length(duplicate_note_columns) != 2) {
  stop("Expected exactly two columns named higher_better_notes.")
}
source_names[duplicate_note_columns] <- c(
  "effect_direction_label_raw",
  "higher_better_notes"
)

blank_columns <- which(is.na(source_names) | trimws(source_names) == "")
if (length(blank_columns) > 0) {
  source_names[blank_columns] <- paste0("blank_column_", blank_columns)
}

clean_names <- clean_column_names(source_names)

column_name_crosswalk <- tibble(
  position = seq_along(names(db_raw)),
  source_name = names(db_raw),
  resolved_name = source_names,
  clean_name = clean_names
)

names(db_raw) <- clean_names

blank_clean_names <- clean_names[blank_columns]
if (length(blank_clean_names) > 0) {
  blank_has_data <- vapply(
    db_raw[blank_clean_names],
    function(x) any(!is.na(x) & trimws(as.character(x)) != ""),
    logical(1)
  )
  if (any(blank_has_data)) {
    stop("An unnamed source column contains data and requires manual naming.")
  }
  db_raw <- db_raw %>% select(-all_of(blank_clean_names))
}

text:
2.5 Formulas used to harmonize central tendency

2.5.1 Standard error and standard deviation
When a study provides an SD but no SE, we use
[ SE = . ]
When a study provides an SE but no SD, we rearrange the same identity:
[ SD = SE. ]
The extraction sheet contains some rows where the entered SE equals mean / sqrt(n) rather than SD / sqrt(n). The raw entry is retained, the problem is flagged, and the harmonized SE is recalculated from the SD.


2.5.2 Median and interquartile range
For groups reporting the first quartile (Q_1), median (M), third quartile (Q_3), and sample size (n), the mean is estimated with the Luo et al. (Luo et al. 2018) estimator for this reporting scenario:
[ w = 0.7 + , ]
[ = w() + (1-w)M. ]
The SD is estimated using Wan et al. (Wan et al. 2014):
[ = {2^{-1}()}, ]
where (^{-1}) is the standard-normal quantile function (qnorm() in R). These estimators require (n ) and assume that using normal-distribution quantiles is reasonable. We therefore create, but do not automatically act on, a skewness-review flag.

luo_iqr_mean <- function(q1, median, q3, n) {
  weight <- 0.7 + 0.39 / n
  weight * ((q1 + q3) / 2) + (1 - weight) * median
}

wan_iqr_sd <- function(q1, q3, n) {
  denominator <- 2 * stats::qnorm((0.75 * n - 0.125) / (n + 0.25))
  (q3 - q1) / denominator
}

approximately_equal <- function(observed, expected) {
  !is.na(observed) & !is.na(expected) &
    abs(observed - expected) <= pmax(0.01, 0.02 * abs(expected))
}

derive_arm_statistics <- function(data, arm) {
  raw_mean <- data[[paste0(arm, "_mean_raw")]]
  raw_sd <- data[[paste0(arm, "_sd_raw")]]
  raw_n <- data[[paste0(arm, "_n_raw")]]
  raw_se <- data[[paste0(arm, "_se_raw")]]
  raw_ci <- data[[paste0(arm, "_ci_raw")]]
  median <- data[[paste0(arm, "_median_raw")]]
  q1 <- data[[paste0(arm, "_q1_raw")]]
  q3 <- data[[paste0(arm, "_q3_raw")]]

  complete_iqr <- !is.na(q1) & !is.na(median) & !is.na(q3) &
    !is.na(raw_n) & raw_n >= 5

  iqr_order_valid <- !complete_iqr | (q1 <= median & median <= q3)
  if (any(!iqr_order_valid)) {
    stop("Invalid Q1 <= median <= Q3 ordering in the ", arm, " arm.")
  }

  estimated_mean <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  estimated_sd <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  estimated_mean[complete_iqr] <- luo_iqr_mean(
    q1[complete_iqr], median[complete_iqr], q3[complete_iqr], raw_n[complete_iqr]
  )
  estimated_sd[complete_iqr] <- wan_iqr_sd(
    q1[complete_iqr], q3[complete_iqr], raw_n[complete_iqr]
  )

  mean_pre_minimum <- ifelse(!is.na(raw_mean), raw_mean, estimated_mean)
  mean_source <- case_when(
    !is.na(raw_mean) ~ "raw_mean",
    is.na(raw_mean) & complete_iqr ~ "luo_2018_q1_median_q3",
    TRUE ~ "missing"
  )

  # Prefer an extracted SD. If it is absent, prefer a reported SE over
  # estimating an SD from quartiles.
  sd_from_se <- raw_se * sqrt(raw_n)
  sd_clean <- case_when(
    !is.na(raw_sd) ~ raw_sd,
    is.na(raw_sd) & !is.na(raw_se) & !is.na(raw_n) & raw_n > 0 ~ sd_from_se,
    is.na(raw_sd) & complete_iqr ~ estimated_sd,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )

  assumed_sqrt_mean <- !is.na(raw_sd) & !is.na(data$stat_comment) &
    grepl("sqrt\\s*\\(mean\\)", tolower(data$stat_comment), perl = TRUE)

  sd_source <- case_when(
    !is.na(raw_sd) & assumed_sqrt_mean ~ "assumed_sqrt_mean_in_extraction",
    !is.na(raw_sd) ~ "raw_sd",
    is.na(raw_sd) & !is.na(raw_se) & !is.na(raw_n) & raw_n > 0 ~ "se_times_sqrt_n",
    is.na(raw_sd) & complete_iqr ~ "wan_2014_q1_q3",
    TRUE ~ "missing"
  )

  expected_se <- sd_clean / sqrt(raw_n)
  se_consistent <- approximately_equal(raw_se, expected_se)
  mean_based_se <- raw_mean / sqrt(raw_n)
  se_matches_mean_formula <- approximately_equal(raw_se, mean_based_se) &
    !se_consistent

  se_clean <- case_when(
    !is.na(raw_se) & se_consistent ~ raw_se,
    !is.na(expected_se) ~ expected_se,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_
  )

  se_source <- case_when(
    !is.na(raw_se) & se_consistent ~ "raw_se_verified",
    !is.na(raw_se) & !se_consistent & !is.na(expected_se) ~ "recalculated_from_sd",
    is.na(raw_se) & !is.na(expected_se) ~ "sd_div_sqrt_n",
    TRUE ~ "missing"
  )

  skewness_statistic <- ifelse(
    complete_iqr & q3 > q1,
    abs((q1 + q3 - 2 * median) / (q3 - q1)),
    NA_real_
  )
  skewness_critical_value <- ifelse(
    complete_iqr,
    2.65 / sqrt(raw_n) - 6 / raw_n^2,
    NA_real_
  )

  data[[paste0(arm, "_n")]] <- raw_n
  data[[paste0(arm, "_mean_pre_minimum")]] <- mean_pre_minimum
  data[[paste0(arm, "_mean_source")]] <- mean_source
  data[[paste0(arm, "_sd")]] <- sd_clean
  data[[paste0(arm, "_sd_source")]] <- sd_source
  data[[paste0(arm, "_se")]] <- se_clean
  data[[paste0(arm, "_se_source")]] <- se_source
  data[[paste0(arm, "_ci")]] <- raw_ci
  data[[paste0(arm, "_iqr_complete")]] <- complete_iqr
  data[[paste0(arm, "_iqr_all_zero")]] <- complete_iqr & q1 == 0 & median == 0 & q3 == 0
  data[[paste0(arm, "_iqr_skewness_statistic")]] <- skewness_statistic
  data[[paste0(arm, "_iqr_skewness_review")]] <- !is.na(skewness_statistic) &
    skewness_statistic >= skewness_critical_value
  data[[paste0(arm, "_sd_assumed_sqrt_mean")]] <- assumed_sqrt_mean
  data[[paste0(arm, "_se_inconsistent_with_sd")]] <- !is.na(raw_se) &
    !is.na(expected_se) & !se_consistent
  data[[paste0(arm, "_se_matches_mean_over_sqrt_n")]] <- se_matches_mean_formula

  data
}

db <- derive_arm_statistics(db, "c")
db <- derive_arm_statistics(db, "ex")

The current c_ci and ex_ci columns contain no values, and a single CI column would not show whether it contains a lower limit, upper limit, width, or half-width. We therefore do not infer SE from those columns. If confidence intervals are added later, we will store lower and upper limits separately and document the confidence level before applying a conversion such as

apply_crosswalk <- function(data, variable, crosswalk) {
  raw_column <- paste0(variable, "_raw")
  data[[raw_column]] <- data[[variable]]

  map <- crosswalk[crosswalk$variable == variable, , drop = FALSE]
  raw_character <- trimws(as.character(data[[raw_column]]))
  matched <- match(raw_character, map$raw_value)
  data[[variable]] <- ifelse(
    is.na(raw_character),
    NA_character_,
    ifelse(is.na(matched), NA_character_, map$clean_value[matched])
  )
  data
}

2.7 Primary minimum-mean rule
For outcomes measured in seconds or counts, the primary analysis uses 1 as the minimum biologically meaningful mean. The pre-rule mean remains in c_mean_pre_minimum or ex_mean_pre_minimum; the canonical c_mean and ex_mean columns contain the primary-analysis values.
This rule changes means only. It does not modify SDs. Sensitivity analyses using the unfloored positive means and alternative handling of exact zeros will be implemented in the lnRR chapter.

minimum_rule_units <- c("seconds", "count")

db <- db %>%
  mutate(
    c_mean_minimum_rule_applied = data_units %in% minimum_rule_units &
      !is.na(c_mean_pre_minimum) & c_mean_pre_minimum < 1,
    ex_mean_minimum_rule_applied = data_units %in% minimum_rule_units &
      !is.na(ex_mean_pre_minimum) & ex_mean_pre_minimum < 1,
    c_mean = ifelse(c_mean_minimum_rule_applied, 1, c_mean_pre_minimum),
    ex_mean = ifelse(ex_mean_minimum_rule_applied, 1, ex_mean_pre_minimum),
    minimum_mean_rule_applied = c_mean_minimum_rule_applied |
      ex_mean_minimum_rule_applied,
    zero_quartile_sensitivity_exclusion = c_iqr_all_zero | ex_iqr_all_zero
  )

text:
2.8 Parse maternal and exposure moderators

2.8.1 Dam age
dam_age mixes numeric text with values such as 16 weeks. The numeric component is stored in dam_age_weeks; the source text is retained in dam_age_raw. Missingness remains explicit.


2.8.2 Frequency
Frequency is not forced into a single number. We preserve the text and create lower limit, upper limit, midpoint, and reporting-format columns. For the primary categorical representation:

a range at or below 20,000 Hz is audible;
a range entirely above 20,000 Hz is ultrasound;
a range crossing the 20,000-Hz boundary is mixed_or_boundary;
missing frequency is not_reported.

The midpoint is retained for exploratory analysis only because a point frequency and a broad range are not equivalent exposures.

extract_numbers <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || trimws(x) == "") return(numeric(0))
  normalized <- gsub(",", "", x, fixed = TRUE)
  hits <- regmatches(
    normalized,
    gregexpr("[0-9]+(?:\\.[0-9]+)?", normalized, perl = TRUE)
  )[[1]]
  if (length(hits) == 1 && hits[1] == "") return(numeric(0))
  as.numeric(hits)
}

db$dam_age_raw <- db$dam_age
db$dam_age_weeks <- vapply(
  as.character(db$dam_age_raw),
  function(x) {
    values <- extract_numbers(x)
    if (length(values) == 0) NA_real_ else values[1]
  },
  numeric(1)
)

db$frequency_hz_raw <- db$frequency_hz
frequency_values <- lapply(as.character(db$frequency_hz_raw), extract_numbers)

db$frequency_min_hz <- vapply(
  frequency_values,
  function(x) if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else x[1],
  numeric(1)
)
db$frequency_max_hz <- vapply(
  frequency_values,
  function(x) if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else x[length(x)],
  numeric(1)
)
db$frequency_mid_hz <- rowMeans(
  cbind(db$frequency_min_hz, db$frequency_max_hz),
  na.rm = FALSE
)
db$frequency_format <- case_when(
  is.na(db$frequency_min_hz) ~ "not_reported",
  db$frequency_min_hz != db$frequency_max_hz ~ "range",
  TRUE ~ "point"
)
db$acoustic_band_from_frequency <- case_when(
  is.na(db$frequency_min_hz) | is.na(db$frequency_max_hz) ~ "not_reported",
  db$frequency_max_hz <= 20000 ~ "audible",
  db$frequency_min_hz > 20000 ~ "ultrasound",
  TRUE ~ "mixed_or_boundary"
)

2.9 Row-level audit of central statistics
The audit file below is in long format: each effect size has one control row and one experimental row. It shows the source values, derived values, method labels, minimum-rule decisions, and review flags.

make_arm_audit <- function(data, arm, label) {
  arm_code <- arm
  tibble(
    study_id = data$study_id,
    es_id = data$es_id,
    n_raw = data[[paste0(arm_code, "_n_raw")]],
    n_final = data[[paste0(arm_code, "_n")]],
    mean_raw = data[[paste0(arm_code, "_mean_raw")]],

2.10 Moderator dictionary and feasibility
Moderator feasibility is assessed using both numbers of effect sizes and numbers of independent studies. A level with many effect sizes from one study does not provide the same evidence as a level represented across several studies.

moderator_dictionary <- tribble(
  ~variable, ~domain, ~kind, ~units, ~planned_use, ~definition_or_caution,
  "sp_latin", "offspring_biology", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Species; assess imbalance by study",
  "strain", "offspring_biology", "categorical", NA, "exploratory", "Do not collapse strains without biological justification",
  "dam_age_weeks", "maternal", "numeric", "weeks", "exploratory", "Substantial missingness expected",
  "gest_window", "prenatal_exposure", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Combined gestational exposure window",
  "gest_early", "prenatal_exposure", "binary", NA, "descriptive", "Exposure includes early gestation",
  "gest_mid", "prenatal_exposure", "binary", NA, "descriptive", "Exposure includes mid gestation",
  "gest_late", "prenatal_exposure", "binary", NA, "descriptive", "Exposure includes late gestation",
  "exposure_span_d", "prenatal_exposure", "numeric", "days", "candidate", "Total exposure span",
  "exposure_type", "prenatal_exposure", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Continuous versus intermittent",
  "exposure_session_duration_h", "prenatal_exposure", "numeric", "hours", "candidate", "Duration per exposure session",
  "noise_type", "prenatal_exposure", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Source/noise class from extraction",
  "acoustic_band_from_frequency", "prenatal_exposure", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Derived from reported frequency limits",
  "frequency_mid_hz", "prenatal_exposure", "numeric", "Hz", "exploratory", "Point and range midpoint are not equivalent",
  "frequency_format", "prenatal_exposure", "categorical", NA, "descriptive", "Point, range, or not reported",
  "loudness_db", "prenatal_exposure", "numeric", "dB", "candidate", "Confirm comparability of acoustic weighting/reference",
  "control_conditions", "methodological", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Ambient sound, silence, or unclear",
  "offspring_sex", "offspring_biology", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Male, female, or mixed",
  "offspring_age_d", "offspring_biology", "numeric", "days", "candidate", "Age at outcome assessment",
  "outcome_type", "outcome", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Anxiety or depression",
  "assay_type", "outcome", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Behavioural assay",
  "measurement_variable", "outcome", "categorical", NA, "exploratory", "Many levels; likely sparse",
  "data_type", "methodological", "categorical", NA, "candidate", "Count, time, latency, percentage, or index",
  "measurement_timing", "methodological", "categorical", NA, "exploratory", "Light phase, dark phase, or not reported"
)

is_present <- function(x) !is.na(x) & trimws(as.character(x)) != ""

moderator_feasibility <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(moderator_dictionary)), function(i) {
  variable <- moderator_dictionary$variable[i]
  x <- db[[variable]]
  present <- is_present(x)
  tibble(
    variable = variable,
    domain = moderator_dictionary$domain[i],
    kind = moderator_dictionary$kind[i],
    planned_use = moderator_dictionary$planned_use[i],
    n_effect_sizes = sum(present),
    n_studies = n_distinct(db$study_id[present]),
    n_unique_values = n_distinct(x[present]),
    n_missing = sum(!present)
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

categorical_moderators <- moderator_dictionary %>%
  filter(kind %in% c("categorical", "binary")) %>%
  pull(variable)

moderator_level_counts <- lapply(categorical_moderators, function(variable) {
  data.frame(
    study_id = db$study_id,
    level = as.character(db[[variable]]),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(level) & trimws(level) != "") %>%
    group_by(level) %>%
    summarise(
      n_effect_sizes = n(),
      n_studies = n_distinct(study_id),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(variable = variable, .before = 1)
}) %>% bind_rows()

moderator_feasibility %>%
  arrange(domain, variable) %>%
  knitr::kable()

validation_summary <- tribble(
  ~check, ~severity, ~n_failed, ~interpretation,
  "es_id is present and unique", "error", sum(is.na(db$es_id)) + sum(duplicated(db$es_id)), "Each effect size must have one row",
  "study_id is present", "error", sum(is.na(db$study_id) | trimws(db$study_id) == ""), "Every effect size must link to a study",
  "sample sizes are positive", "error", sum(is.na(db$c_n) | db$c_n <= 0 | is.na(db$ex_n) | db$ex_n <= 0), "lnRR variance requires valid n",
  "analysis means are complete", "error", sum(is.na(db$c_mean_final) | is.na(db$ex_mean_final)), "All arms require a mean for lnRR",
  "analysis SDs are complete", "error", sum(is.na(db$c_sd_final) | is.na(db$ex_sd_final)), "All arms require an SD for lnRR variance",
  "analysis SEs are complete", "error", sum(is.na(db$c_se_final) | is.na(db$ex_se_final)), "Every arm should now have a directly reported or SD-derived SE",
  "analysis means are positive", "error", sum(db$c_mean_final <= 0 | db$ex_mean_final <= 0, na.rm = TRUE), "lnRR requires positive means after the zero correction",
  "con_id / ex_id present", "error", sum(is.na(db$con_id) | is.na(db$ex_id)), "Needed to model dependence among effect sizes",
  "recalculated SE matches extraction team's *_se_analysis", "review", sum(se_crosscheck$abs_diff >= 0.001), "This chapter's SD-derived SE should reproduce the pre-computed *_se_analysis columns to within rounding",
  "zero SD alongside zero-mean correction", "review", sum(db$c_sd_zero_review | db$ex_sd_zero_review), "es184 / es190: control arm has no reported spread",
  "frequency values failed to parse", "review", sum(!is.na(db$frequency_Hz) & db$frequency_format == "not_reported"), "Check the frequency text for an unexpected format",
  "dam_age missing", "review", sum(is.na(db$dam_age_weeks)), "Expected: dam_age was only reported for a subset of studies"
) %>%
  mutate(status = ifelse(n_failed == 0, "pass", ifelse(severity == "error", "fail", "review"))) %>%
  select(check, severity, status, n_failed, interpretation)

title: 3  Effect-size calculation: lnRR
text:
3.1 The log response ratio
This project uses the log response ratio (lnRR), the natural logarithm of the ratio of the treatment mean to the control mean (Hedges et al. 1999; Lajeunesse 2015), as agreed in the protocol.
Every treatment-control pair in this dataset uses independent animals (confirmed in the protocol deviation review: “the control and exposed animals are distinct for every comparison”), so the same independent-arm formula applies to all 207 effect sizes - there is no paired/dependent-design branch to handle.
Positive lnRR is not yet interpretable on its own: it only means “the exposed-group mean was higher than the control-group mean” for a given outcome, and outcomes are scored in both directions (e.g., more time in the open arms of an elevated-plus maze is less anxiety-like behaviour, while more immobility in a forced-swim test is more depression-like behaviour). The next step harmonizes this so the sign is comparable across outcomes.

luo_iqr_mean <- function(q1, median, q3, n) {
  weight <- 0.7 + 0.39 / n
  weight * ((q1 + q3) / 2) + (1 - weight) * median
}

wan_iqr_sd <- function(q1, q3, n) {
  denominator <- 2 * stats::qnorm((0.75 * n - 0.125) / (n + 0.25))
  (q3 - q1) / denominator
}

Only one situation needs a mean or SD calculated from another statistic: the 18 abramova_2023_biopsy rows tagged median_iqr_deferred_to_r above, where the study reported the median, Q1, and Q3 for each arm but not the mean or SD. These use the Luo et al. (Luo et al. 2018) mean estimator and the Wan et al. (Wan et al. 2014) SD estimator agreed for this project. Every other row already has a final mean and SD (by whichever route the table above shows), so this chapter passes those through unchanged.
The SE is handled the same way for every row, including the 18 above: if the study (or the extraction team, from digitised or emailed data) directly reported an SE, that value is used unchanged; otherwise SE = SD / sqrt(n) is calculated from the mean/SD obtained above. This is the same relationship the extraction team used to build *_se_analysis - the validation step at the end of this section confirms the two agree.

finish_arm_statistics <- function(data, arm) {
  n        <- data[[paste0(arm, "_n")]]
  mean_x   <- data[[paste0(arm, "_mean")]]
  sd_x     <- data[[paste0(arm, "_sd")]]
  se_x     <- data[[paste0(arm, "_se")]]
  median_x <- data[[paste0(arm, "_median")]]
  q1       <- data[[paste0(arm, "_q1")]]
  q3       <- data[[paste0(arm, "_q3")]]
  method   <- data$stat_derivation_method

  from_iqr <- method == "median_iqr_deferred_to_r"
  if (any(from_iqr & !(is.na(q1) | is.na(median_x) | is.na(q3)) & !(q1 <= median_x & median_x <= q3))) {
    stop("Invalid Q1 <= median <= Q3 ordering in the ", arm, " arm.")
  }

  # Mean: calculated only for the median/IQR rows; passed through otherwise.
  mean_final <- mean_x
  mean_final[from_iqr] <- luo_iqr_mean(q1[from_iqr], median_x[from_iqr], q3[from_iqr], n[from_iqr])
  mean_source <- ifelse(from_iqr, "luo_2018_median_iqr", method)

  # SD: calculated for the median/IQR rows (Wan et al.), and for the small
  # group of rows where a study reported an SE but no SD (SD = SE * sqrt(n),
  # 13 rows in `uygur_2010_aphyhun`, `uygur_2011_ankarauniv`, and
  # `abramova_2024_devneur`); passed through otherwise (including the
  # assumed-SD-equals-sqrt(mean) and raw-data-derived rows, which are already
  # final numbers, just obtained upstream of this chapter).
  sd_final <- sd_x
  sd_final[from_iqr] <- wan_iqr_sd(q1[from_iqr], q3[from_iqr], n[from_iqr])
  sd_from_se <- is.na(sd_final) & !is.na(se_x)
  sd_final[sd_from_se] <- se_x[sd_from_se] * sqrt(n[sd_from_se])
  sd_source <- case_when(
    from_iqr ~ "wan_2014_median_iqr",
    sd_from_se ~ paste0(method, "_sd_from_se_times_sqrt_n"),
    TRUE ~ method
  )

  # SE: use a directly reported/digitised/emailed SE unchanged; otherwise
  # calculate it from the mean/SD obtained above. This is computed for every
  # row, including the 18 median/IQR rows, which had no SE at all before.
  se_reported <- !is.na(se_x)
  se_final <- ifelse(se_reported, se_x, sd_final / sqrt(n))
  se_source <- ifelse(se_reported, paste0(method, "_se_reported"), paste0(method, "_se_computed_sd_over_sqrt_n"))

  data[[paste0(arm, "_mean_final")]] <- mean_final
  data[[paste0(arm, "_mean_source")]] <- mean_source
  data[[paste0(arm, "_sd_final")]] <- sd_final
  data[[paste0(arm, "_sd_source")]] <- sd_source
  data[[paste0(arm, "_se_final")]] <- se_final
  data[[paste0(arm, "_se_source")]] <- se_source
  data[[paste0(arm, "_mean_pre_zero_correction")]] <- mean_final
  data
}

text:
2.4 Exact-zero continuity correction
The Luo estimator returns an exact zero mean whenever a study reports Q1 = median = Q3 = 0 (a “floor effect”, e.g. no head-out inspections recorded for any animal in that arm). log(0) is undefined, so the primary lnRR analysis replaces an exact-zero analysis mean with 0.9 times the smallest positive analysis mean observed in the same outcome stratum (assay_type, measurement_variable, data_type, data_units), matching the correction rule already agreed for this project. The uncorrected value is kept in *_mean_pre_zero_correction; the SD is not changed by this rule.

zero_correction_strata <- c("assay_type", "measurement_variable", "data_type", "data_units")

zero_correction_values <- db %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(zero_correction_strata))) %>%
  summarise(
    zero_correction_reference_mean = {
      candidates <- c(c_mean_pre_zero_correction, ex_mean_pre_zero_correction)
      positive <- candidates[is.finite(candidates) & candidates > 0]
      if (length(positive) == 0) NA_real_ else min(positive)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(zero_correction_primary_09 = 0.9 * zero_correction_reference_mean)

db <- db %>%
  # Drop these columns first (rather than relying on left_join to overwrite
  # them) so this chunk gives the same result whether it is run once or
  # re-run later in the same R session - re-running it without this line
  # would leave the old columns in place and add new ones with a ".y"
  # suffix instead, since the columns already exist in `db` after the first
  # run.
  select(-any_of(c("zero_correction_reference_mean", "zero_correction_primary_09"))) %>%
  left_join(zero_correction_values, by = zero_correction_strata) %>%
  mutate(
    c_mean_exact_zero = !is.na(c_mean_pre_zero_correction) & c_mean_pre_zero_correction == 0,
    ex_mean_exact_zero = !is.na(ex_mean_pre_zero_correction) & ex_mean_pre_zero_correction == 0,
    c_mean_final = ifelse(c_mean_exact_zero, zero_correction_primary_09, c_mean_final),
    ex_mean_final = ifelse(ex_mean_exact_zero, zero_correction_primary_09, ex_mean_final),
    c_mean_source = ifelse(c_mean_exact_zero, paste0(c_mean_source, "_zero_corrected"), c_mean_source),
    ex_mean_source = ifelse(ex_mean_exact_zero, paste0(ex_mean_source, "_zero_corrected"), ex_mean_source),
    c_sd_zero_review = c_mean_exact_zero & (is.na(c_sd_final) | c_sd_final == 0),
    ex_sd_zero_review = ex_mean_exact_zero & (is.na(ex_sd_final) | ex_sd_final == 0)
  )

db %>%
  filter(c_mean_exact_zero | ex_mean_exact_zero) %>%
  select(
    study_id, es_id, assay_type, measurement_variable,
    c_mean_pre_zero_correction, c_mean_final, c_sd_final,
    ex_mean_pre_zero_correction, ex_mean_final, ex_sd_final,
    zero_correction_reference_mean
  ) %>%

2.5 Parse the remaining free-text fields
frequency_Hz is reported as a mix of single values and ranges (e.g. "20,000-45,000"). It is not collapsed to one number; the categorical acoustic band is what feeds the moderator models, and the midpoint is kept only for exploratory use. A range is audible at or below 20,000 Hz, ultrasound when entirely above 20,000 Hz, and mixed_or_boundary when it crosses that line, following the same rule already used in the extraction review.
dam_age and loudness_dB are already numeric in the v10 file, so they are used as is (aliasing dam_age to dam_age_weeks to match the moderator dictionary’s naming). dam_age remains missing for 118/207 rows, as anticipated during extraction.

extract_numbers <- function(x) {
  if (is.na(x) || trimws(x) == "") return(numeric(0))
  normalized <- gsub(",", "", x, fixed = TRUE)
  hits <- regmatches(
    normalized,
    gregexpr("[0-9]+(?:\\.[0-9]+)?", normalized, perl = TRUE)
  )[[1]]
  if (length(hits) == 1 && hits[1] == "") return(numeric(0))
  as.numeric(hits)
}

frequency_values <- lapply(as.character(db$frequency_Hz), extract_numbers)

db$frequency_min_hz <- vapply(frequency_values, function(x) if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else x[1], numeric(1))
db$frequency_max_hz <- vapply(frequency_values, function(x) if (length(x) == 0) NA_real_ else x[length(x)], numeric(1))
db$frequency_mid_hz <- rowMeans(cbind(db$frequency_min_hz, db$frequency_max_hz), na.rm = FALSE)
db$frequency_format <- case_when(
  is.na(db$frequency_min_hz) ~ "not_reported",
  db$frequency_min_hz != db$frequency_max_hz ~ "range",
  TRUE ~ "point"
)
db$acoustic_band_from_frequency <- case_when(
  is.na(db$frequency_min_hz) | is.na(db$frequency_max_hz) ~ "not_reported",
  db$frequency_max_hz <= 20000 ~ "audible",
  db$frequency_min_hz > 20000 ~ "ultrasound",
  TRUE ~ "mixed_or_boundary"
)

db$dam_age_weeks <- db$dam_age

  count(frequency_Hz, frequency_format, acoustic_band_from_frequency) %>%

2.6 Dependence-structure identifiers
Several effect sizes share a control group: shared_control == "yes" for 103/207 rows, and in some studies (e.g. barzegar_2014_hippo) one control group (con_id) is reused against several different exposed cohorts (ex_id). That reuse is exactly the kind of dependence the protocol deviation addendum flags for the variance-covariance structure rather than the extraction sheet itself. Because con_id already identifies which rows share a control group’s data - and, in this dataset, is finer-grained than grouping by ex_id alone would be - Chapters 3-5 build the variance-covariance matrix by clustering on con_id. This section just aliases it as dependency_cluster_id so later chapters read one clearly-named column instead of re-deriving the same idea, and checks that no cluster keys are missing.

if (any(is.na(db$con_id)) || any(is.na(db$ex_id))) {

title: 3  Effect-size calculation: lnRR
text:
NoteFormula



\[
\ln RR = \ln\left(\frac{M_T}{M_C}\right) + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{SD_T^2}{N_T M_T^2} - \frac{SD_C^2}{N_C M_C^2}\right)
\]
where \(M_T\), \(SD_T\), \(N_T\) are the mean, standard deviation, and sample size of the noise-exposed group, and \(M_C\), \(SD_C\), \(N_C\) are the same for the control group. This is the bias-corrected estimator implemented by metafor::escalc(measure = "ROM").








NoteA note on the “robust estimator” wording in the protocol





The protocol cites Nakagawa et al. (Nakagawa et al. 2023) for a “robust estimator of lnRR”. That paper (Ecology Letters, 2023) proposes a method specifically for meta-analyses with a substantial share of missing standard deviations, using sample-size-based weighting instead of the usual SD-based sampling variance for the affected rows. In this dataset only 31/207 rows needed a derived SD (Chapter 1), and all 207 have a usable SD after that step, so the standard escalc(measure = "ROM") estimator above is used throughout. If a future update to this dataset has many more missing SDs, revisit this decision and implement the Nakagawa et al. (2023) weighting instead.

title: 3  Effect-size calculation: lnRR
section: 3.2 Calculate lnRR and its sampling variance
text:
3.2 Calculate lnRR and its sampling variance

es <- metafor::escalc(
  measure = "ROM",
  m1i = ex_mean_final, sd1i = ex_sd_final, n1i = ex_n,
  m2i = c_mean_final,  sd2i = c_sd_final,  n2i = c_n,
  data = db
)

es <- es %>%
  rename(lnrr_raw = yi, lnrr_var = vi) %>%
  mutate(
    lnrr_se = sqrt(lnrr_var),
    higher_better = trimws(higher_better),
    lnrr_harm = ifelse(tolower(higher_better) == "yes", -lnrr_raw, lnrr_raw)
  )

if (any(!es$higher_better %in% c("Yes", "No"))) {
  stop("higher_better must be exactly 'Yes' or 'No' for every row.")
}
if (any(is.na(es$lnrr_raw) | is.na(es$lnrr_var))) {
  stop("escalc produced a missing lnRR or variance; check the input means/SDs/n.")
}

tibble(
  effect_sizes = nrow(es),
  studies = n_distinct(es$study_id),
  flipped_for_direction = sum(tolower(es$higher_better) == "yes")

ggplot(es, aes(x = lnrr_harm)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "#477AA8", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "#B24745") +
  labs(x = "Harmonized lnRR", y = "Number of effect sizes") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)




Distribution of harmonized lnRR across all 207 effect sizes. Positive values indicate more anxiety- or depression-like behaviour under maternal chronic noise exposure.





ggplot(es, aes(x = lnrr_se, y = lnrr_harm)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "#477AA8") +
  labs(x = "Standard error of lnRR", y = "Harmonized lnRR") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)




lnRR against its standard error. Points far to the right with a small effect size are the most influential on the funnel-plot check in Chapter 5.

title: 5  Uni-moderators
text:
5.1 Approach
Each candidate moderator from the protocol (biological factors: species, sex, age; methodological factors: exposure timing/intensity, noise type, outcome type, assay type) is fit one at a time (“uni-moderator”), using the same random-effects structure and cohort-level variance-covariance matrix as the overall-effect model in Chapter 3. Fitting moderators one at a time, rather than in one large multi-moderator model, matches the protocol and keeps every model interpretable given the sample size (207 effect sizes from 16 studies).
For categorical moderators, a level is only modelled if it has at least 5 effect sizes; levels below that are dropped and reported as such, rather than silently included in an unstable estimate. The number of studies contributing to each level is always shown next to the number of effect sizes, because several effect sizes from one study are weaker evidence than the same count spread across studies. For categorical moderators with 3 or more surviving levels, pairwise contrasts between levels are also reported, unadjusted for multiple comparisons (as descriptive contrasts, not confirmatory tests). For continuous moderators, the model is a simple linear meta-regression.
offspring_age_class (juvenile / adolescent / adult) is intentionally not in this main set - per the protocol deviation addendum, it is restricted to descriptive summaries and sensitivity analyses and does not replace offspring_age_d as the primary age moderator. It is fit at the end of this chapter, labelled as a sensitivity analysis, not a primary result.

# Keep only levels with at least min_k effect sizes. The VCV matrix does not
# need to be subset here because it is rebuilt from the filtered data (see
# fit_categorical()) rather than sliced from the full matrix.
filter_low_k <- function(dat, moderator, min_k = 5) {
  dat <- dat %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[moderator]]))
  dat[[moderator]] <- droplevels(as.factor(dat[[moderator]]))

  level_counts <- dat %>%
    group_by(level = .data[[moderator]]) %>%
    summarise(n_effect_sizes = n(), n_studies = n_distinct(study_id), .groups = "drop")

  keep_levels <- level_counts %>% filter(n_effect_sizes >= min_k) %>% pull(level)
  dat_f <- dat %>% filter(.data[[moderator]] %in% keep_levels)
  dat_f[[moderator]] <- droplevels(dat_f[[moderator]])

  list(data = dat_f, level_counts = level_counts)
}

fit_categorical <- function(es, moderator, min_k = 5) {
  filtered <- filter_low_k(es, moderator, min_k)
  dat <- filtered$data
  if (nrow(dat) < 5 || nlevels(dat[[moderator]]) < 2) return(list(level_counts = filtered$level_counts, model = NULL))

  V <- metafor::vcalc(vi = lnrr_var, cluster = dependency_cluster_id, obs = es_id, rho = 0.5, data = dat)

  mod <- metafor::rma.mv(
    yi = lnrr_harm,
    V = V,
    mods = as.formula(paste0("~ ", moderator)),
    random = list(~1 | study_id, ~1 | es_id, ~1 | strain),
    test = "t",
    method = "REML",
    sparse = TRUE,
    data = dat
  )

  plot <- orchaRd::orchard_plot(
    mod,
    mod = moderator,
    group = "study_id",
    xlab = "lnRR (harmonized)",
    flip = TRUE
  )

  tukey <- NULL
  if (nlevels(dat[[moderator]]) >= 3) {
    mod_nointercept <- metafor::rma.mv(
      yi = lnrr_harm,
      V = V,
      mods = as.formula(paste0("~ ", moderator, " - 1")),
      random = list(~1 | study_id, ~1 | es_id, ~1 | strain),
      test = "t",
      method = "REML",
      sparse = TRUE,
      data = dat
    )
    k <- nlevels(dat[[moderator]])
    K <- multcomp::contrMat(rep(1, k), type = "Tukey")
    colnames(K) <- names(coef(mod_nointercept))
    tukey <- summary(multcomp::glht(mod_nointercept, linfct = K), test = multcomp::adjusted("none"))
  }

  list(level_counts = filtered$level_counts, model = mod, r2 = orchaRd::r2_ml(mod), plot = plot, tukey = tukey)
}

fit_continuous <- function(es, moderator, min_n = 10, min_studies = 3) {
  dat <- es %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[moderator]]))
  if (nrow(dat) < min_n || n_distinct(dat$study_id) < min_studies) {
    return(list(n_effect_sizes = nrow(dat), n_studies = n_distinct(dat$study_id), model = NULL))
  }

  V <- metafor::vcalc(vi = lnrr_var, cluster = dependency_cluster_id, obs = es_id, rho = 0.5, data = dat)

  mod <- metafor::rma.mv(
    yi = lnrr_harm,
    V = V,
    mods = as.formula(paste0("~ ", moderator)),
    random = list(~1 | study_id, ~1 | es_id, ~1 | strain),
    test = "t",
    method = "REML",
    sparse = TRUE,
    data = dat
  )

  plot <- orchaRd::bubble_plot(
    mod,
    mod = moderator,
    group = "study_id",
    xlab = moderator,
    ylab = "lnRR (harmonized)"
  )

  list(n_effect_sizes = nrow(dat), n_studies = n_distinct(dat$study_id), model = mod, r2 = orchaRd::r2_ml(mod), plot = plot)
}

title: 6  Publication bias
text:
6.1 Approach
Following the protocol, publication bias is assessed with a funnel plot and an Egger-style regression test (Nakagawa et al. 2022). Because lnRR and its sampling variance are mathematically linked (the variance depends on the same means used in the numerator), regressing directly on the standard error can itself create a spurious asymmetry. Following the recommendation in Nakagawa et al. (Nakagawa et al. 2022), the Egger-type test below uses a sample-size-based precision proxy, \(\sqrt{1/n_{ex} + 1/n_c}\), as the moderator in the same multilevel model used for the overall effect, rather than the standard error itself.
Both diagnostics are exploratory: heterogeneity is expected to be substantial and many effect sizes are not independent, both of which make classic publication-bias tests less reliable than in a simple two-group design. They are reported for transparency and to flag whether a sensitivity analysis is warranted, not as a definitive test.

title: 8  Leave-one-out sensitivity analysis
text:
8.1 Approach
The protocol commits to sensitivity analyses when a diagnostic (publication bias, or variation in CRIME-Q quality ratings) flags a concern. Chapter 5’s funnel plot and Egger-type regression noted that “excluding one study at a time” would be the appropriate follow-up, so this chapter carries that out.
There is a second, more specific reason to run this here: four of the 16 included studies - abramova_2020_genpath, abramova_2021_front, abramova_2023_biopsy, and abramova_2024_devneur - are from the same author and lab, and together they contribute 118 of the 207 effect sizes (57%), far more than their 25% share of studies. A standard one-study-at-a-time leave-one-out would not, by itself, reveal a pattern shared across all four of that lab’s papers, since removing any single one still leaves the other three in the model. There is also a third, narrower question left open from Chapter 1: two effect sizes (es184, es190) had their control-arm mean and SD corrected to a non-zero floor value because the study reported an exact Q1 = median = Q3 = 0, and that correction was flagged there for review rather than acted on. This chapter runs three checks:
All three are exploratory/diagnostic, same as Chapter 5: they describe how sensitive the pooled estimate is to these exclusions, not a hypothesis test with its own pass/fail criterion.

If the estimate and its confidence interval stay similar with the Abramova-lab studies removed - same direction, overlapping intervals - the overall result does not depend on that lab’s contribution. If the estimate moves substantially, or crosses from excluding zero to including it (or vice versa), that is a genuine limitation to report: more than half of this dataset’s effect sizes come from one author/lab, and the pooled result is at least partly a reflection of their specific methods and animals rather than the broader literature. Either way, report both numbers together rather than only the “all studies” or only the “excluding Abramova” figure on its own - if the significance conclusion depends on this one inclusion/exclusion decision, that dependency is itself part of the result.






NoteReading the I2_strain column here



If I2_strain drops sharply once the Abramova-lab studies are excluded, that is a modelling side-effect, not a new finding about strain: Abramova’s four studies span two strains (Sprague-Dawley and Wistar), so they are the main source of within-strain replication across independent studies. Without them, most remaining strains appear in only one study each, so strain and study_id become almost indistinguishable to the model, and REML can assign that shared variance entirely to study_id instead of splitting it. It would not be evidence that strain stopped mattering biologically.

8.4 Combined check: excluding the exact-zero-corrected effect sizes
Two effect sizes, es184 and es190 (abramova_2023_biopsy), had Q1 = median = Q3 = 0 reported for their control arm. Chapter 1’s Luo/Wan estimators return an exact-zero mean and SD for a row like that, which log(0) cannot handle, so the mean was replaced with 0.9 times the smallest positive mean in the same outcome stratum before lnRR was calculated (Chapter 1’s exact-zero continuity correction). That correction was flagged there as needing review rather than acted on; this is that review.

exact_zero_es <- c("es184", "es190")

es_no_exact_zero <- es %>% filter(!as.character(es_id) %in% exact_zero_es)

if (nrow(es) - nrow(es_no_exact_zero) != length(exact_zero_es)) {
  stop(
    "Expected to remove exactly ", length(exact_zero_es), " effect size(s) (",
    paste(exact_zero_es, collapse = ", "), "), but removed ", nrow(es) - nrow(es_no_exact_zero),
    ". Check that these es_id values still exist in db_effect_sizes.csv."
  )
}

VCV_no_exact_zero <- metafor::vcalc(
  vi = lnrr_var,
  cluster = dependency_cluster_id,
  obs = es_id,

Only 2 of 207 effect sizes are affected, so a large shift here would be a stronger signal than the same shift would be in the Abramova check above - two rows should not be able to move a 207-row pooled estimate much unless their corrected values are doing a lot of work. If the estimate and CI are essentially unchanged, that resolves Chapter 1’s open review item: the correction is not consequential enough to need a different fix. If they shift noticeably, that is worth a closer look at whether 0.9 times the smallest positive stratum mean is the right choice for these two rows specifically, rather than a rule to apply everywhere.
